message.content:
The sea usually looks **blue**—the water absorbs longer‑wave colors (red, orange) more strongly than shorter ones (green, blue), so when sunlight hits it most of what we see is scattered back as blue light.  

Of course, its hue changes with conditions:

| Factor | Effect |
|--------|--------|
| Depth & clarity | Deeper, clearer waters appear darker blues or even deep indigo; shallow or murky areas may look greenish or brownish. |
| Sun angle | At sunrise/sunset the sea often takes on pinks, oranges, or purples because of reflected sky tones. |
| Algae / phytoplankton | High concentrations give a greener tint. |
| Sediment / runoff | Can make coastal seas muddy or yellowish. |

So while “blue” is the classic description, the actual color depends largely on where you’re looking from!
